title: Walk times with one long walk
observableEvidence: Computes the mean and median of a data set with an outlier and chooses the median as the better typical value because the outlier pulls the mean.
prompt: Seven students timed their walks to school, in minutes: 12, 8, 43, 11, 15, 10, 13. Find the mean and the median, then choose the measure that better describes a typical walk time for this group and the reason.
solutionRepresentation: Sum: 12 + 8 + 43 + 11 + 15 + 10 + 13 = 112, so the mean is 112 / 7 = 16 minutes. Ordered: 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 43; the 4th value, 12 minutes, is the median. Only 1 of the 7 times is above 16, because the 43-minute walk pulls the mean up, so the median, 12, better describes a typical walk.
solutionMethod: Compute both measures, then check which one sits among most of the data when one value is far from the rest.

deterministicValidator.canonicalAnswer: Mean walk time in minutes: 16; Median walk time in minutes: 12; Better measure of a typical walk: The median, because the 43-minute walk pulls the mean above most times
acceptedAnswers: Mean walk time in minutes: 16; Median walk time in minutes: 12; Better measure of a typical walk: The median, because the 43-minute walk pulls the mean above most times
deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Structured fields. Each number field accepts any equal value written as an integer, decimal, fraction or mixed number; the choice field must match its correct option. No partial credit.

fields.label: Better measure of a typical walk

options.label: The mean, because it uses every walk time
The range, because it shows the spread
The median, because the 43-minute walk pulls the mean above most times
Either one, because they are always equal

hintSteps.prompt: For the mean, add all seven times and divide by 7. For the median, order the times and take the middle one.
hintSteps.question: What is the total of all seven walk times?

hintSteps.prompt: Compare each measure with the actual times. A typical value should sit among most of the data.
hintSteps.question: How many of the seven students walked for longer than the mean you found?

hintSteps.prompt: A different group of five has times 5, 6, 7, 8 and 29 minutes. The mean is 55 / 5 = 11, which is more than four of the five times, while the median, 7, sits among them.
hintSteps.question: Does the same thing happen in this group, and which measure sits among most of the walk times?

forbiddenLeakagePatterns: pulls the mean above most times
